claims.text: MoNbTaTiW is a refractory high-entropy alloy suitable for consideration in high-temperature applications.
Refractory high-entropy alloys have poor oxidation resistance at high temperature.
Unprotected MoNbTaTiW forms non-protective or rapidly growing oxides during high-temperature exposure.
A Si-20Cr-20Fe coating can be prepared on MoNbTaTiW by a fused slurry method.
The fused-slurry Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating can effectively prevent oxidation of MoNbTaTiW under high-temperature oxidation conditions.
A coating composition can be optimized using density functional theory and thermodynamic modeling to establish favorable oxidation free energies and diffusion properties.
Such computational optimization will produce a coating superior in oxidation resistance to both untreated and conventionally coated refractory alloys.
The proposed method is intended for oxidative exposure at approximately 1000–1430 °C.
The optimized coating will favor in situ formation of a slow-growing, adherent Al2O3 or Cr2O3 layer.
A slow-growing Al2O3 or Cr2O3 layer acts as an effective diffusion barrier to oxygen.
During high-temperature oxidation, an element from a silicide coating can diffuse into the MoNbTaTiW substrate.
After oxidation, a coated MoNbTaTiW surface can consist of an outer oxide layer and an inner silicide layer.
Diffusion of selected coating elements into the substrate generates a continuous protective oxide scale.
The resulting oxide scale limits oxygen ingress and thereby retards further oxidation.
The computationally optimized coating will reduce oxidation-related weight gain relative to an untreated alloy.
The computationally optimized coating will reduce oxidation rate relative to a conventional fused-slurry Si-20Cr-20Fe coating.
The computationally optimized coating will form a more stable and adherent protective layer than the conventional coating.
The protective effect may diminish when temperature or environmental conditions fall outside the modeled regime.
